one_line: Ganga king of Odisha who reshaped sacred kingship around Lord Jagannath amid 13th‑century warfare and state reform.

appearance.age_look: early 40s, tall and athletic with a disciplined warrior’s build
appearance.face: oval face, medium-brown Odishan complexion, straight nose, sharp jawline, neatly trimmed moustache and short beard along the jaw, calm yet intense eyes with a steady, composed expression
appearance.hair: thick black hair drawn back into a high, tight topknot at the crown, sides smoothed with oil, adorned by a simple gold circlet featuring a small central wheel (chakra) motif above the forehead
appearance.costume: royal Ganga-period attire: a cream-white, finely woven cotton dhoti wrapped securely to the ankles with a narrow maroon border, a fitted pale-gold long-sleeved angarakha-style upper garment crossing over the chest and tied at the side, and over it a rich maroon silk uttariya draped from left shoulder across chest and around the back like a sash; the cloth is plain with subtle woven texture, not flashy; he wears a broad gold necklace with a small Jagannath-disc pendant, two modest gold armlets on the upper arms, simple gold bangles at the wrists, and leather sandals; no bare torso, garments fully cover chest and legs in dignified royal modesty
appearance.signature: a long, slightly curved Odishan sword with a plain steel blade, a simple iron hilt wrapped in dark brown leather, and a functional wooden scabbard hanging from a practical belt at his left hip, carried as a symbol of protective kingship rather than ostentatious display

ref_desc: Anangabhima Deva III is a tall, medium-brown Ganga king with a neat moustache and jawline beard, black hair in a high topknot and gold circlet, wearing cream dhoti, pale-gold angarakha, maroon silk uttariya, gold Jagannath necklace, leather sandals, and carrying a plain curved sword at his left hip in a wooden scabbard, all in a cream, maroon, pale gold, dark brown, and black palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Anangabhima Deva III: a tall, athletic Odishan king in his early 40s with an oval, medium-brown face, sharp jawline, straight nose, calm intense eyes, neat moustache and short beard along the jaw, and thick black hair pulled into a high topknot. On his head sits a simple gold circlet with a small central wheel motif. He is fully clothed in 13th-century Ganga-period royal attire: a cream-white cotton dhoti wrapped securely to the ankles with a narrow maroon border, a fitted pale-gold long-sleeved angarakha-style upper garment crossing over the chest and tied at the side, and a rich maroon silk uttariya draped from his left shoulder across the chest and around his back like a sash, all with subtle woven texture but no ornate patterns. He wears a broad gold necklace with a small Jagannath-disc pendant, modest gold armlets on both upper arms, simple gold bangles at the wrists, and plain leather sandals, with his torso and legs fully covered in dignified, modest clothing. At his left hip hangs his signature weapon: a long, slightly curved plain steel sword with a simple iron hilt wrapped in dark brown leather, sheathed in a functional wooden scabbard attached to a practical belt. Show him front-facing with a composed, resolute expression, emphasizing consistent face, high topknot and circlet, the cream dhoti, pale-gold angarakha, maroon uttariya, gold jewellery, sandals, and the curved sword and scabbard in a cream, maroon, pale gold, dark brown, and black colour scheme.
